clue.text: Spoilt children ask me around in the morning — this is symbolic

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters sit on either side of the next piece
spoilt things are ruined or messed up, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning hours

explanation.surface: A grumpy parent complains that indulged kids pester them first thing every morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoilt' rearranges CHILDREN ASK ME; 'around' wraps those letters about AM, which goes in after the opening H.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossed tools are the emblem of Soviet communism, a symbol by definition; the clue's whole phrase points at it.

clue.text: Searched around area inhabited by ghosts

indicators.note: around says the first word's letters go about the next piece

parts.note: to have hunted for something is to have searched for it

explanation.surface: Someone combed a district reputed to be full of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A house visited by spirits of the dead is said to be haunted; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Civvies leaving unit fuming on the way back?

indicators.note: on the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
leaving here means left showing within the words, so the letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A soldier storms off from an angry regiment, swapping uniform for ordinary clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Civvies leaving' was trimmed to 'Civvies': only that word names the clothes, and 'leaving' is the signal that the letters sit inside 'unit fuming', read 'on the way back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary clothing worn by someone usually in uniform, such as an off-duty officer, is called by this Anglo-Indian word.

clue.text: Unfortunately one comes across one making savings

indicators.note: across here means stretched over and around, so one piece encloses another
something that turns out unfortunately has gone awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sadly, someone stumbles on another person who is busy cutting costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes across' reads as 'meets', but 'comes' is part of the fodder for 'Unfortunately' and 'across' wraps that around the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuts made to spending are savings; both words describe money kept back by thrift.

clue.text: Legal case resulting from instruction to shoot

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit brought in court, as in bringing an ... against someone
the word a film director calls out to start the cameras rolling

explanation.surface: A lawsuit arises from an order to fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit is a legal action, and a director's call to begin filming is the same word.

clue.text: Belief is lacking in discretion, possibly

indicators.note: possibly flags that the remaining letters may be arranged another way
lacking in says the following short word is missing from the longer one

explanation.surface: A faith is said to be short on tact, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' takes IS out of DISCRETION, leaving DCRETION, and 'possibly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine is a body of teaching held as true, a belief or tenet.

clue.text: Times will support oddly viable mountain dweller

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece goes beneath the one it holds up
oddly picks every other letter of the word

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper promises to back an unusually workable creature of the peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' here takes the alternate letters I, B, E of 'viable'. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild goat lives on high alpine crags, so it is a mountain dweller by habitat.

clue.text: Mostly benevolent western sultanate imprisoning second family member

indicators.note: imprisoning says the letters hold the next piece inside them
mostly means nearly all of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: a benevolent person is kind
Oman is a sultanate in the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A largely charitable Gulf monarchy is detaining someone for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoning' holds the second's letter inside everything before it, so it lands mid-word rather than inside the sultanate alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A female relative is a member of one's family; the word means a woman of the same kin.

clue.text: Enduring being outside with no vote

indicators.note: with no says a letter is taken away

parts.note: something external is located outside
X is the mark made on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: Someone endures life as an outsider, denied the franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes X, the ballot-paper cross, from EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that lasts forever endures without end; enduring and everlasting are synonyms.

clue.text: Open in advance

definitions.meaning: frank and candid, not hiding anything
paid before goods or services are delivered

explanation.surface: A shop that is open ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank is being candid, and a payment made beforehand is made at the outset; one word covers both.

clue.text: Purge lists seen in church

indicators.note: seen in says the next piece appears inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship lists when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: A clear-out of rolls of names is spotted at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lists' looks like a noun for registers but is the verb meaning tilts, as a ship does. 'seen in' puts it inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid of impurities, which is to clean thoroughly; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Go red after short excursion and flag

indicators.note: after puts the first piece behind the one that follows it in the clue
short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
to colour is to blush or go red

explanation.surface: Someone blushes after a brief outing and loses heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like the verb meaning tire; here it is the banner. 'after' sets the blush behind the outing cut 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner of three broad stripes, like the French one, is a three-coloured flag.

clue.text: Small pale creature

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: A little washed-out animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked water bird is one kind of creature; the definition names it by class.

clue.text: Lies bound to be rejected outside European Commission

indicators.note: outside says the first word's letters wrap round the next piece
rejected means thrown back, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: something bound is tied up

explanation.surface: Someone's untruths are certain to be thrown out by Brussels officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain' but means fastened. 'outside' wraps it round the Commission, and 'to be rejected' turns the whole of that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lies and trickery amount to dishonesty; telling falsehoods is the practice of misleading.

clue.text: These days may be more frequent before the start of autumn

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: something more common is seen more frequently

indicators.note: the start of picks out only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Present times may grow busier ahead of the beginning of fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The dating system CE marks the present epoch, the age we live in now, hence these days.

clue.text: Let a student know without ceremony?

parts.note: with the later word, to let someone know is to tell them
L is the learner plate, a student driver

explanation.surface: Telling a pupil something casually, with no fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let ... know' together give INFORM, with 'a student' in between, so the clue reads INFORM A L.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual, relaxed behaviour skips formality and ritual, so it is done without any ceremony.

clue.text: Is Her Majesty supporting Hammond perhaps for manager?

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting pieces go beneath the one they hold up

parts.note: the Hammond is a well-known make of electric organ
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A question whether the monarch is backing the politician Philip Hammond for a top job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammond' suggests the British politician but is the Hammond organ. 'supporting' places IS ER below ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges and runs things is an organiser; a manager does the same job.

clue.text: Fancy international reference ignoring leader

indicators.note: ignoring leader says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an allusion is an indirect reference

explanation.surface: A worldly citation leaves out its first letter, rather fancifully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring leader' takes the A off ALLUSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a figment of imagination, a false impression or fantasy.

clue.text: So, I'm dressed in new lace underwear!

indicators.note: new means remade, so these letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman shows off her latest lacy lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: SO I'M sits 'dressed in' the lace, and 'new' rearranges all eight letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless top worn under clothing is a piece of lingerie, hence underwear.

clue.text: Copper charges people helping barmen in Ireland

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rates are prices or charges

explanation.surface: A policeman bills the assistants who work behind an Irish bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal's chemical symbol. In Irish usage a pub's assistant barman has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Ireland an assistant to the publican or barman in a pub is traditionally given this name.

clue.text: Drink, for example prior to backing call for meal

indicators.note: prior to puts the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a gong is struck to summon diners to a meal

explanation.surface: A beverage served before the dinner bell is answered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the dinner signal, and 'prior to' puts the example abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas beverage of egg, milk and spirits is a type of drink.

clue.text: Fine skills must underpin good racing vehicles

indicators.note: in a down answer the underpinning pieces go below the one above them

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
arts are skills or crafts

explanation.surface: Fine skills must support good motorsport vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must underpin' puts OK ARTS below G in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Small open motor vehicles raced around tracks, often by beginners, are a kind of racing car.

clue.text: Literature problem raised in sort of test paper

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A literary difficulty is brought up in a school exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SUM upwards to read MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Indicator paper dipped in a solution to test acidity or alkalinity is called by this name.

clue.text: Go berserk and scream

definitions.meaning: to run ..., behaving wildly and violently
an informal word for a very funny person or thing

explanation.surface: Lose control and shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a violent uproar, and a hilarious person can be called a laugh or a scream.

clue.text: University working with means of lifting national standard

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a jack lifts a car to change a wheel

explanation.surface: A university is busy with ways of raising its national benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' suggests a level of quality but means a flag, the British one here.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this one is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Left a clean plate at the dump, occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only alternate letters are kept

explanation.surface: Someone finished every scrap at the rubbish tip, now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing all the food served is leaving a clean plate; the phrasal verb means consumed entirely.

clue.text: Authorisation in advance

definitions.meaning: a permit, a document letting one go somewhere
an amorous approach, as when making a move on someone

explanation.surface: Permission granted beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is a written authorisation, and an amorous approach is an advance made at someone.

clue.text: Anthem a girl used to keep bearers of gifts

indicators.note: the words keep, that is hold, the letters within them

explanation.surface: A girl's song was once kept by gift-givers, as if a carol.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men brought gold, frankincense and myrrh to the infant Jesus, so carried gifts.

clue.text: Therapist's regret returning after service

indicators.note: after puts the first piece behind the one that follows it in the clue

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist feels remorse coming home after church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay. 'returning' reverses the regret, and 'after' sets it behind the service.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rubs and kneads muscles to relieve pain is a kind of therapist.

clue.text: Brilliant beaches — makes an effort to include parking and flag

parts.note: star means outstanding, as in a star turn
sands are beaches

indicators.note: to include says the next piece goes inside the one before

parts.note: to try is to make an effort
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Glittering shores where people strive to fit in a car park and a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts P inside TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The national flag of the United States is popularly known by this name.
